key_insight: Enforcing linear completeness enables PIML convergence, addressing a learning-induced error term that may persist under mesh refinement when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient substructure-based finite element analysis by learning reusable numerical shape functions while preserving conformity and improving convergence reliability.
method: Train neural networks to map material distributions or element geometries to numerical shape functions.
Bound PIML error using finite element discretization error and network generalization error.
Reconstruct transition-matrix columns using linear displacement constraints to ensure linear completeness.
evidence_signal: The paper derives H1- and L2-norm convergence results, and numerical experiments support optimal convergence rates, good generalization, and numerical stability.
watch_item: Linear completeness addresses convergence consistency, but network generalization error still contributes to the total error bound.
paper_title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
